articleTitle: Online Crime Reporting System for Digital Forensics
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The occurrence of unlawful acts, commonly known as crimes, is on the rise in our society. However, the process of reporting such crimes to law enforcement agencies through traditional procedures is extremely complicated and time-consuming for victims. Additionally, law enforcement agencies face difficulties in manually investigating and maintaining criminal records. To address these issues, an online crime reporting system can be implemented, which will not only simplify the process but also keep the users informed of any updates or instructions from law enforcement agencies regarding their complaints. Such a system will facilitate communication between the law enforcement agencies and victims, ultimately enhancing security in the community. On the other hand, there is a need to implement an interactive platform to help the investigator manage crime investigation processes using tools such as statistical dashboard, database management tools, a crime type classifier and also a tool to extract valuable information from the crime documents using a powerful technique such as natural Languages processing. It can be stated that the proposed system has demonstrated satisfactory outcomes.

articleTitle: Fake Product Detection Using Blockchain Using QR Code
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Issues such as service duplication, inadequate departmental coordination, and a lack of standardization often plague supply chain management due to a lack of transparency. Counterfeiting has become increasingly prevalent, making it extremely difficult to visually identify counterfeit products. Counterfeiters cause significant challenges for legitimate firms, yet far too many people have no idea of the entire amount of counterfeit items’ influence on brands. Various approaches have been developed in the past to address the challenge of product counterfeiting. The most popular methods are using RFID tags, Artificial Intelligence, QR Code based systems, etc. Each of them had a few disadvantages such as the QR Code can be copied from a genuine product and placed on a fake product, artificial intelligence uses CNN and machine learning which needs heavy computational power and so on. The idea of this paper is to improve detection of fake products by linking product SN with customer ID in the seller’s system. This is achieved with Blockchain technology which ensures the identification and traceability of real products through QR Code. Blockchain based systems, makes everything decentralized. One of its main advantages is that the recorded data is difficult to change without the consent of all parties concerned which makes the data extremely secure and protected from all vulnerabilities.

articleTitle: Weedspedia: Deep Learning-Based Approach for Weed Detection using R-CNN, YoloV3 and Centernet
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Weed identification is a crucial undertaking in agriculture, where management and identification of weed growth in fields need to be addressed through deep learning algorithms. This study uses the Region-Based Convolutional Neural Network (R-CNN), Yolo, and Centernet object recognition algorithms to identify objects in images. This study also proposes a novel method for weed identification based on weed size. Numerous image-processing applications, including those for healthcare, traffic analysis, and agriculture, frequently use R-CNN. The suggested technique provides a practical and affordable answer for weed identification in precision agriculture. Herbicide use by farmers can be reduced as a result of being able to more precisely identify and control weed growth. Identification of weeds aids in weed growth control, which can harm natural ecosystems, compete with crops, diminish yields, and increase maintenance costs. The methodology of measuring the length and breadth of a weed detected by R-CNN requires extra processing stages, which aid in understanding the growth and subsequent steps required to eliminate weeds dependent on the growth of the weeds. Researchers often begin by gathering a sizable collection of photos of various weed species to construct a deep learning model for weed identification. The paper focus on identification of weed using 3 pre trained models followed by growth prediction to take necessary steps in agricultural land.

articleTitle: Role of Artificial Intelligence in Criminal Investigation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: With the advent of technology, criminals are developing more sophisticated methods for criminal activities and the use of Artificial intelligence (AI) has the capacity to address this phenomenon. The role of AI in improving the effectiveness of criminal investigation is discussed in the present study as intelligent scrutiny of crime allows the law enforcement bodies to understand the vast dynamics of criminal activities and it provides potential answers about why how and when about occurrence of crime. Four such technologies-crime prediction, facial recognition, video investigation and neuroimaging are very much into use by criminal investigation bodies. In the current study the use of AI with these technologies in criminal investigation is focused upon. At last, there is always some scope for improvement and the same applies to the use of AI, regarding this the discussion and suggestions are mentioned in this study so that artificial intelligence can be better applied to criminal investigation methods and as this field is in a state of development further research and studies are recommended to derive the maximum benefits from technology.

articleTitle: A Novel Set Theory Rule based Hybrid Feature Selection Techniques for Efficient Anomaly Detection System in IoT Edge
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In the modern Internet of Things (IoT) era, smart gadgets are deployed over various network infrastructures with less reliability, opening up a wide range of new attacks and anomalies. Many machine learning (ML) based investigations have proposed different intrusion detection models (IDS) to detect anomalies. However, the multidimensional and vast nature of IoT data makes ML models ineffective. Thus, feature selection is an essential processing step to improve the system’s overall performance when dealing with large dataset. This paper proposes a novel set theory rule-based feature selection method to upgrade the performance of the anomaly detection model. Three prominent feature selection techniques, namely Chi-square, Particle swarm optimization, and XG boost algorithm, are used for optimum feature selection. Six different rules are generated using union and intersection operators. The features obtained from the developed rule are trained using the random forest (RF) and Multi-layer perception (MLP) algorithms with the UNSW-NB15 dataset. Based on the complete empirical analysis, random forest with the Rule 1 feature subset has the highest detection accuracy of 94.17%.

articleTitle: Quantum Secure Multiparty Summation Based on Quantum Walks
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: We propose an efficient Quantum Secure Multiparty Summation protocol based on quantum walk states. It enables multiple participants to find the sum of all the data without revealing it to anyone else. With the help of quantum walks, we can achieve this with fewer quantum resources and minimal communication costs. The protocol also requires a semi-honest third party (TP) to facilitate the protocol. The semi-honest TP follows the protocol but attacks passively. Finally, we prove its correctness and security, making it a viable solution for quantum secure multiparty summation.

articleTitle: Enhancing Darknet Traffic Analysis through Top Ranked Feature Selection Methods
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Darknet traffic classification explores the benefits of employing the top-ranked feature selection approach in order to reduce dimensionality, enhance computational efficiency, and improve model interpretability. The study utilizes various filter-based techniques, including Information Gain (IG), Gain Ratio (GR), Correlation (CR), ChiSquared, and Anova, to progressively select features. These selected features are then evaluated using a bagging classifier on an imbalanced dataset. The findings demonstrate that the Anova technique surpasses other methods, achieving an accuracy of 98.1156% while reducing the feature count by 31%. This highlights the effectiveness of filter-based techniques in identifying informative features while maintaining high accuracy, thereby offering potential enhancements to computational efficiency and model interpretability.

articleTitle: Attention U-Net: A Deep Learning Approach for Breast Cancer Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: One of the main causes of death for women globally is breast cancer. Early discovery can reduce the frequency of early deaths. Breast ultrasound images can help in diagnosis and treatment planning by helping to categories different types of breast cancer. To segment breast cancer pictures in this study, we employed an Attention U-Net. A deep learning model for picture segmentation is called the Attention U-Net. We used a dataset of 780 breast ultrasound pictures divided into three classes-normal, benign, and malignant-to train the Attention U-Net. The mean IoU, precision, recall, and F1 scores for the Attention U-Net were 0.840,0.815,0.848, and 0.831 respectively. These outcomes are comparable to those of other cutting-edge techniques for segmenting breast cancer. The findings of this study indicate that the Attention U-Net is a potential technique for segmenting breast cancer. The great accuracy that the Attention U-Net can attain can assist to increase the precision of diagnosis and treatment planning

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Resource-Constrained Cryptographic Devices: A Lightweight Countermeasure Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Foundations of cryptography revolve around employing mathematically robust crypto-algorithms to ensure the data security. Nonetheless, even though these algorithms possess mathematical security, their implementation remains susceptible to non-invasive attacks. In response, Threshold Implementation (TI) has surfaced as a robust safeguard against such vulnerabilities. However, the introduction of TI in cryptographic devices increases hardware complexity, making it unsuitable for devices with limited resources. Therefore, it is crucial to develop efficient and impactful countermeasure strategies specifically designed for these designs. In this paper, our proposal introduces an Arbiter Physical Unclonable Function (A-PUF) based True Random Number Generator (TRNG) to obfuscate the intermediate values within the register. Additionally, we employ a pre-charge countermeasure to obfuscate combinational switching activities and a neutralizing countermeasure to further conceal register switching activities. Using a rolled (iterative) structure of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES), this countermeasure is implemented on a 65nm Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA). To evaluate the effectiveness of this countermeasure, we conduct a comparative analysis in terms of security strength and area consumption, comparing it with conventional design approaches.

articleTitle: On the Study of Partial Qubit Hamiltonian for Efficient Molecular Simulation Using Variational Quantum Eigensolvers
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Quantum computing is being extensively used in quantum chemistry, especially in simulating simple molecules and evaluating properties like the ground state energy, dipole moment, etc. The transformation of a molecular Hamiltonian from the fermionic space to the qubit space provides us with a series of Pauli strings and the energy calculation involves the evaluation of the expectation values of all these individual strings. This introduces a major bottleneck for applications of VQEs in quantum chemistry. Unlike the fermionic Hamiltonian, the terms in a qubit Hamiltonian are additive and the present paper exploits this property to describe a new approach for extracting information from the partial qubit Hamiltonian of simple molecules to design more efficient variational quantum eigensolvers. In the partial (qubit) Hamiltonian approach (PHA), the qubit Hamiltonian is studied term-by-term to understand their relative contributions to the overall energy, and a partial Hamiltonian is constructed with fewer Pauli strings that can resolve the entire Hamiltonian. With PHA, we can simulate molecules at a much lower computational cost with a truncated Hamiltonian. Additionally, the outcomes of the measurements with PHA quench the error due to noise introduced by the quantum circuits. We have also demonstrated the application of PHA as an initialization technique, where the simple partial Hamiltonian can be used to find an optimal starting point for a more complex system.

articleTitle: Linear Bit-by-Bit Encoding and its Application
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In computer terminology, encoding is the process of placing a specific code or a sequence of characters (in the form of certain symbols, punctuation, numbers, or letters) into a specific format for storage or efficient transmission. Today, quantum computers have been pitched to deliver the computing power necessary to solve computationally complex problems, that are currently thought to be difficult for classical computers. With the arrival of quantum machine learning algorithms, it has become important to explore unique methods of encoding and compressing data with qubits. In this paper, we will explore the possibility of linear bit-by-bit data compression in the state vector of a multi-qubit system. We will achieve this, by looking at a brief introduction to the topic, a possible way by which we could encode bits in a state vector and whether this system of encoding can be applied to a real time system. We will also elaborate on a possible application through a proposed protocol for secure communication, and suggest a further line of discussion on this topic.

articleTitle: Exhilarating Growth in Education Through Artificial Intelligence
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In the early decades of the $21^{\text {st }}$ century, AI and statistical machine learning has subjugated the field and these technologies has proven highly successful in helping to solve challenging situations throughout academics and industry. The methodology used in this paper is studying the various research articles thus, draws the attention of the readers to know about how technology is affecting and revolutionizing the educational field across the world. The contribution of this study is showing the use of technology in the components of education like better universal success, learning process, clarity, skills and lifelong learning. In this paper it is also found that the technology can fill the gap between the traditional classroom and advanced learning. Some challenges regarding technological education are addressed in this paper such as data privacy and security, cost and resource constraint, ethical consideration and human centered approach. In conclusion, the advanced technology of AI and machine learning are enhancing the learning aspect and develops the curiosity to learn in a modern way but with due care and fairness.

articleTitle: Transforming Greenhouse Horticulture Using Artificial Intelligence and Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In todays, to cope with the problems caused by the rising worldwide need for basic foodstuffs, it is vital to discover ecologically friendly solutions. Vegetable crops may be grown all year long, regardless of the climate or season, thanks to horticulture. The production process for horticulture may be categorized as an unstructured & extremely complicated system that is influenced by the climate, environment, pests, disease, herbicides, nutrients, pricing, & combinations of these numerous aspects. Digital twins might be seen as the beginning of a new era in data-driven & intelligent greenhouse horticulture. The study of the article is about the advancement of horticulture via the application of reducing technologies, especially digital technology. The purpose of this article is to offer, with the need for technology, the vital information that producers may utilize to harvest a range of crops to reap the most rewards. This study describes the outcomes of structured use of the Digital Twin application throughout greenhouse horticulture, as Artificial Intelligence applies to learn approaches throughout its applications to proclaim the best cost-effective & maximal benefit for the agriculturist. Based on the analysis, the article identifies challenges and suggests a few vital recommendations for future work. The findings of this study on the efficiency of concept in the growth of concentrated fruits and vegetables are examined.

articleTitle: Sustainable Development Practices of Big Data in Corporate Social Responsibility
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The research paper discusses the utilization of Big Data Technologies for the advancement of economic and environmental responsibilities which are regarded as the major components of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR). The CSR model is highly prevailing and is the factual need that has to be fitted in every corporate which exercises its business practices on the land of earth. From brand image to legal liability, CSR has a wide role to play. With the inculcation of big data technologies for computation of CSR, the loophole to escape from responsibility has been reduced. Furthermore, the paper discusses how Big Data is used for the multiple components of CSR. A concept of tech interacted CSR is the prevailing need of the hour. The study focuses on the analysis of secondary sources. The paper also gives suggestions for the better application of the CSR model and effective CSR strategy to enhance the productivity and brand image of the company. Results have shown that for the different major components of CSR, the different subset of Big Data Technology is used for proper functioning. Lastly, this paper concludes with the idea of positive gain from the innovative use of Big Data Technology for resting responsibilities under the ambit of CSR.

articleTitle: A New Approach of Machine Learning And Deep Learning Algorithms Based Crop Yield Prediction
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The science and art of raising plants and wild animals is called agriculture. India’s agriculture ranks second in the world and its agricultural areas make up 60.45% of the country’s land. The Indian economy mainly supports the agriculture and agro industrial sectors. Crop rotation, soil consistency, weather and temperature, precipitation, and other factors all affect crop growth. The most important thing is the composition of the soil, which includes nitrogen, phosphate and potassium. Ongoing work in this area includes product selection models using machine learning techniques (random forests, tree pruning, artificial neural networks). In this paper, a recommendation model has been developed using deep learning techniques to obtain accurate information about the amount of suitable land and their added value, as well as crop estimation. It provides better accuracy than existing models. Existing data are reviewed to help farmers estimate crop yields. Take soil and climate differences into account to estimate yields. This project introduces a Python-based system that uses cunning techniques to predict profits while using limited resources. This work combines SVM machine learning algorithm with LSTM and RNN deep learning algorithms.

Author Keywords: SVM machine learning algorithm LSTM and RNN deep learning algorithm

articleTitle: Embedded Device Forensics with a Case Study of Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The ever-evolving digital forensics is now coping up with latest trends in cyber-attacks. Among them Embedded Device forensics is a trending topic and that needs more research and development. Today, with the prevalence of miniaturized computers, the possibility of launching a cyber-attack using a physically hidden device on a premises is a facile task. Embedded device forensics involves identification, data extraction and analysis from miniaturised computers involved in a cyber-crime. This paper includes the research conducted on such a cyber-crime using the most convenient and widely used microcomputer, Raspberry Pi(RPi). In this research, RPi device is used to create a MITM attack and methods for extracting and analysing the suspect device storage media is well explained. Initially the files with evidential artifacts are explained and later the techniques and tools for extracting and analysing these files are explained in detail. The paper also explains the scope of Live Forensics and password recovery in embedded devices. This paper provides an insight for investigators and crime analysts who come across with a case where micro computers are involved as suspect device.

articleTitle: An Efficient Data Storage Technique for User Files in Cloud
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: A remote data storage service provided by cloud providers is known as cloud storage. It substitutes an online-accessible central storage repository for the need for nearby physical storage devices. Cloud storage is efficient due to its wide range of accessibility. An efficient approach for managing file storage in cloud computing environments is presented in this paper. The proposed method utilizes the concept of dividing files into blocks and combining them to generate file hashes using Merkle hash tree (MHT). These file hashes facilitate quick and reliable data integrity verification. Upon transmission of multiple files to the Cloud Service Provider (CSP), a secure storage process is implemented within the cloud environment. The data packets are organized and managed through a $B+$ tree structure. The proposed scheme also supports dynamic file operations. Where users can modify files, and for each modification, a new file hash is generated by merging the block hashes through MHT. By combining the efficiency of Merkle hash tree and B+ tree structures, this proposed system offers a dependable solution for effectively managing files in cloud storage. This method makes a significant contribution to the fields of cloud computing and file management by improving data security, integrity, and accessibility.

articleTitle: Privacy Leaks Via SNI and Certificate Parsing
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In the current digital era, it is essential to provide secure and confidential communication over the internet. In order to accomplish this, Transport Layer Security (TLS), is essential. To create a secure connection, TLS requires the exchange of sensitive data, such as the Server Name Indication (SNI), which could put user privacy at risk. Our study delves into the privacy implications of SNI by creating modules that analyze SNI in the ClientHello Message and TLS certificates. The SNI Parser navigates TLS handshake payload in ClientHello packet, and extracts Server Name Indication. By examining SNI, we gain insights into potential privacy risks associated with unencrypted domain name, which can help in devising effective privacy protection mechanisms. The paper then elucidates how to extract important data from X.509 certificates by providing the server name to the certificate parser that was developed. This research contributes to the comprehension of SNI-related privacy concerns, with the goal of improving user privacy and ensuring a secure online environment.

articleTitle: Qiskit Simulation of CNOT Equivalent Circuits
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: It is known that Controlled NOT (CNOT) operation can generate maximally entangled states which are necessary for quantum communication processes. Further, CNOT is one of the universal two-qubit operators. In this work, we study the various equivalent circuits of CNOT available in the literature. We show the possibility of implementing equivalent circuits in Qiskit.

articleTitle: The Role of AI in Transforming the Dimensions of Governance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: With the advancement in Artificial intelligence (AI), the pursuit for coming in the list of advanced nation become expedient, in which its application in public governance system plays a crucial role. The present study focuses upon the role of $A I$ in improving the existing governance system inculcating Sustainable Development Goal (SDG’s), on which development of the nation is relied upon. The extant literature presents the intervention of technology in the three main components of governance-Decision Making, Fake News Detection, Public Service System. The evaluation also focuses on the scope for effective adoption of technology by presenting recommendations on several grey areas of governance. Eventually, there is always an opportunity for advancement, and this holds true in context of AI. The application of AI in existing governance is still in nascent phase, and because of those further studies and research are encouraged, for extracting maximum advantages from technology. This paper is research opinion article.

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional Quantum Secret Sharing Scheme with Noisy Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Quantum secret sharing (QSS) is a cryptography technique relying on the transmission and manipulation of quantum states to distribute secret information across multiple participants securely. However, quantum systems are susceptible to various types of noise that can compromise their security and reliability. Therefore, it is essential to analyze the influence of noise on QSS to ensure their effectiveness and practicality in real-world quantum communication. This paper studies the impact of various noisy environments on multi-dimensional QSS. Using quantum fidelity, we examine the influence of four noise models: d-phase-flip(dpf), dit-flip(df), amplitude damping(ad), and depolarizing(d). It has been discovered that the fidelity declines with an increase in the noise parameter. Furthermore, the results demonstrate that the efficiency of the QSS protocol differs significantly across distinct noise models.

articleTitle: Dragonfly Algorithm and Variants for Feature Selection: A Review
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Ultimately, the key to successfully analysing real-world problems is to be diligent and thorough. It is important to carefully consider all available data, remove any redundant or unnecessary information, and approach the analysis with an open mind. By doing so, it is possible to gain valuable insights and make informed decisions that can help solve complex real-world problems. By removing redundant, irrelevant, and noisy data, feature selection (FS), a difficult machine learning problem, attempts to lessen the number of features while maintaining a decent degree of classification accuracy. Feature selection is intended to reduce features. This immediately reduces the search space and aids machine learning algorithms in using only the most significant features. A review of Dragonfly algorithms and variants is presented in this paper, emphasizing their main characteristics. Eventually, the conclusion concentrates on the present research on Dragonfly Algorithm, emphasizing its limitations with suggested solutions that lead to future directions

articleTitle: A Concise Polytope Projection Method for ADMM-Assisted LP Decoding of LDPC Codes
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM) has proven to be a highly efficient method for implementing linear programming (LP) decoding for low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes. The projection on the parity polytope is the most time-intensive operation involved in the ADMM-assisted LP decoding. The existing projection methods involve sorting operations or complicated iterations which are difficult to perform by hardware systems. In this paper, an efficient parity-polytope projection algorithm is proposed by mapping the projection problem onto an isomorphic problem of probability simplex. The projection on probability simplex is obtained by utilizing its recurrent structure. This algorithm does not require sorting operations. Each iteration fixes at least one component of the input vector and has straightforward iteration steps. The simulation results show a noticeable reduction in the processing time for obtaining the projection of a given vector. Due to these advantages, it is beneficial for the effective implementation of ADMM-assisted LP decoding systems.

articleTitle: 5G Radio Link Failure Prediction using Quantum Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The next generation of mobile communication networks, 5G, is expected to provide ultra-high-speed, low-latency, and high-reliability wireless communication services. However, radio link failures (RLFs) in 5G networks can degrade network performance and user experience. We present a novel approach for forecasting RLFs in 5G networks using quantum machine learning (QML) in this paper. We employ quantum long short-term memory (QLSTM) with different embedding techniques like Angle embedding, amplitude Embedding, and QAOA embedding in quantum circuits to predict RLFs. We have also merged Quantum circuits to the output of classical Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) to study any improvement over the existing LSTM model. Our approach involves training a QLSTM model using quantum circuits with different embedding techniques to capture the underlying patterns of RLFs. We evaluate our proposed approach on a real-world dataset and the experimental results indicate that our QML approach outperforms classical machine learning techniques in terms of accuracy and loss.

articleTitle: INTELLINEO – An Intelligent Personal Assistant
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Man-made consciousness means to lessen our physical association with electronic devices. Using voice, body language, and other techniques, this technology is currently being developed to enhance our natural interactions with gadgets. Because they enable us to carry out our day-to-day responsibilities with straightforward commands, virtual personal assistants (VPAs) are rapidly gaining popularity. Virtual personal assistants (VPAs) based on various use cases have been developed by numerous multinational corporations, including intelligent devices like Echodot and Alexa. These virtual assistants are having a drawback of security and data theft, So here IntelliNeo, The intelligent personal assistant is designed in such a way that it addresses the security aspects and also allow us to customize our Virtual Personal Assistant (VPA) based on our needs. The methodology of building IntelliNeo involves Voice Acknowledgment, Text Processing, and the added advantage of active background noise cancellation makes our assistant stand out from the competition. Ultimately the purpose of IntelliNeo is to effortlessly automate the daily tasks of its user. Index Terms pyttsx3, PyQt5 tools, Mail Automation, WhatsApp Automation, Text processing, pyautogui, Google Speech Recognition, Microsoft Sapi5.

articleTitle: Internet of Things (IoT) Network Forensic Analysis Using the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B and Open-Source Tools
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The Internet of Things’ (IoT) rapid growth has led to increased concerns regarding network security and the need for effective forensic analysis. This research focuses on investigating the capabilities of the Raspberry Pi 4 Model B and open-source tools for conducting IoT network forensic analysis and collecting digital evidence. The proposed system comprises three components: the IoT Physical Intrusion System Module, the Attack Module, and the Forensic Module. Within the IoT Physical Intrusion System, various attack scenarios, including Denial of Service, SSH Brute Force, and Man in the Middle, were successfully launched. IDS systems such as Wazuh Agent, Suricata, and Fail2ban log application were installed on the Raspberry Pi, effectively identifying IoT threats and providing alerts. The Wazuh Manager, serving as the forensic workstation, received the alerts and facilitated the analysis of attacks, presenting graphical representations. This research demonstrating the practicality of using micro-controller-based device for portable IoT network forensic analysis.

articleTitle: Cybersecurity in the Age of Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The frequency and complexity of cyber assaults have risen considerably in recent years, resulting in major financial losses and reputational harm for both corporations and people. Traditional cybersecurity measures, such as firewalls and encryption, have been insufficient in protecting against these threats. Due to a rise in cyber assaults and data breaches, there is an increased need for effective cybersecurity solutions. With its decentralized nature blockchain technology has come out as a promising option for enhancing cybersecurity. This article investigates how blockchain may be adapted to enhance cybersecurity in areas such as decentralized identity management, safe data storage and sharing, and smart contract security. The article also investigates the potential benefits and barriers of using blockchain in cybersecurity including some cases of successful blockchain implementations in the field of cybersecurity. The report contends that blockchain technology has been able to enhance cybersecurity by offering a secure and transparent platform for digital transactions and data sharing.

articleTitle: Artificial Intelligence in International Arbitration – A Spotlight on the Options
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Over the past several years, the arbitration lawyers and arbitrators have shown an inclination towards the shifting of traditional arbitral processes to artificial intelligence (AI). There are various tools through which AI has been introduced to the arbitral process. Predictive coding is one such method that is currently being employed in international arbitration. There have been discussions going on how arbitration can be benefited from the use of predictive coding and the possible influence it can have on the arbitral process from a dispute resolution standpoint. Despite the discussions on predictive coding and artificial intelligence in international arbitration, very limited literature is available on predictive coding and artificial intelligence for arbitration. Given the importance of predictive coding in international arbitration, this article is aimed at examining the use of predictive coding in international arbitration and how likely it is to influence e-discovery in international arbitration. Analysis of the current scenario indicates that the selection and scope of predictive coding are clearly to be decided by the parties and arbitrators from case-to-case basis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Security in Automobile Edge Computing through Federated Learning and Blockchain
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Vehicular networks that consist of interlinked automobiles and transportation network are prone to cyberattacks due to the increased use of software and the presence of wireless interfaces. To counter these threats, intrusion detection systems can be tailored efficiently. In recent years, there has been significant development in detection of malicious attack traffic through the use of machine learning. However, traditional systems require powerful computing devices to continuously train and update complex network models, which can reduce the efficiency and effectiveness of the system due to resource constraints, untimely updates and dealing with large volumes of data. To address this issue, a cooperative intrusion detection mechanism which had been proposed has been improved with a classification based novel approach, that eases the burden by distributing the training model to distributed edge devices such as connected vehicles and roadside units. The previous approach has a slow response time to the increasing network issues. The proposed work offers a new approach through federated learning with the Extra Trees Classification algorithm. The Extra Trees Classifier performs better than other machine learning models in all aspects. The proposed approach provides a faster response to security threats in automobile edge computing. The use of a distributed federated approach reduces the load on the server while maintaining confidentiality by aggregating models using a blockchain.

articleTitle: Edge Intelligence for Traffic Flow Detection: A Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) are crucial for regulating public transportation, enhancing security, and addressing urban challenges. ITS offers smart guidance to mitigate traffic congestion, minimize environmental impact, and improve overall transport efficiency. In cloud-based ITS, traffic flow detection involves sending video data from edge devices to cloud data centers. However, this approach faces hurdles due to increased monitoring demands. To overcome this, a solution is proposed: employing deep learning on edge nodes. The approach includes a YOLOv4-based vehicle detection model, retrained for multi-object tracking using DeepSORT. Edge computing migrates and installs the detection and tracking systems, ensuring accurate performance at the edge. This approach optimizes traffic flow detection, addressing challenges faced by conventional cloud-based systems.

articleTitle: DQNdot: A Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Object Tracking in UAV-Enabled Aerial Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object tracking enables various applications in diverse domains, such as surveillance, traffic scrutiny, and search and rescue. However, it presents a formidable challenge that necessitates the proficiency to trail objects under arduous circumstances. In this paper, Deep Q Networks on dynamic object tracking (DQNdot) are presented, encompassing the ensuing components: You only look once (YOLOv8) that spotlights objects in video frames, UAV for Multi-Object Tracking (UAVMOT) traces objects in video frames employing the Kalman filter and Hungarian method. Subsequently, the prioritizing module is also advanced to prioritize things that are more liable to be seamlessly traced. This module harnesses a range of factors to appraise the probability of an object being efficaciously traced, such as its size, speed, and appearance. Deep Q network(DQN) endows the capability to trail resourcefully, learn and adapt to the environment. DQNdot has accomplished 92% accuracy of prophesying the results for pursuit. It transcends all the other frameworks as it can proficiently track as many targets as required.

articleTitle: Multi Small Object Detection and Prioritized Tracking for Navy Operations using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Real-time Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) tracking with deep learning improves situational awareness and surveillance capabilities. There is a significant requirement for prioritized tracking and multi-small item detection in the context of Navy operations. To address this, this paper aims to develop an efficient algorithm for locating and tracking small objects, such as ships and people, in extensive maritime surveillance. It proposes an efficient Multi Small Object Detection and Prioritized Tracking (MSOD-PT) approach. This approach aims to develop a reliable and expandable system that enhances situational awareness and helps naval personnel decide by rigorously prioritizing options in actual Navy operation scenarios. The proposed MSOD-PT adopts YOLOv8 for extremely rapid and accurate object identification, allowing for the simultaneous accurate bounding box localization of several small objects. The allocation of computer resources for significant targets is then optimized through the use of DeepSORT, which is utilized to track using specified criteria and give different IDs to things that have been discovered. The targets are then prioritized according to the user’s monitoring needs. The simulation results, which use the AFO dataset, show that the proposed approach is practical and can react to prioritized targets that are not similar. For the custom YOLOv8 model with a confidence score of 0.6, the accuracy is 0.56 for daytime and 0.33 for Night time, but the precision is 0.8 for daytime and 0.6 for Night time.

articleTitle: Analysis and Implementation of Markov Chain-Based Model for Spectrum Defragmentation in Cognitive Radio-Enabled IoT Networks in 5G
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In the context of high demand for high-traffic applications and the increasing need for Internet of Things (IoT) in 5G and beyond 5G networks, Cognitive Radio Networks (CRNs) have emerged as a potential solution due to the scarcity of RF spectrum. However, implementing IoT faces various challenges, including vulnerabilities to changing environmental conditions, efficient bandwidth distribution and utilization, and the high cost of purchasing RF spectrum. To address these challenges, effective spectrum management is crucial, and one aspect of it is spectrum defragmentation. Although it is impossible to completely avoid spectrum fragmentation, efficient spectrum allocation policies can minimize its impact. This paper suggests utilizing Discrete Time Markov Chain (DTMC) models to analyze the busy and idle times of primary users (PUs) in CRNs. The goal is to study the effect of defragmentation on the blocking probability of connections and propose a hybrid proactive-reactive defragmentation model that prioritizes secondary user (SU) traffic while ensuring the confidentiality and integrity of packet data delivery in IoT implementation in 5G. The analytical and simulation results demonstrate the positive impact of defragmentation in reducing the blocking probability and supporting SU traffic.

articleTitle: Secure Key Generation Schemes for Cloud Data Storage
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The secure generation of cryptographic keys holds significant importance in safeguarding the confidentiality, authenticity, and integrity of data stored in the cloud. Traditionally, Key Generation Centers have been trusted with the task of generating partial private keys or private keys to the user, thereby requiring a user to trust a centralized third party. The primary objective focuses on identifying effective methods to enhance the security of key generation processes within existing systems. Additionally, the research takes a deeper look into the possible alternative approaches that eliminate the need for a centralized key generation authority. This study makes a significant contribution to the field of secure key generation by thoroughly examining security advancements within conventional systems. Moreover, it highlights the feasibility of trustless key generation, empowering organizations and individuals to implement more secure key generation mechanisms while reducing their reliance on centralized authorities.

articleTitle: Advancements in Quantum Machine Learning and Quantum Deep Learning: A Comprehensive Review of Algorithms, Challenges, and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: At the nexus of quantum computing and machine learning, quantum machine learning (QML) and quantum deep learning (QDL) have emerged as promising fields. By enhancing computational capabilities and addressing challenging data analysis problems, these approaches have the potential to revolutionise a number of domains by leveraging the special properties of quantum systems, such as superposition and entanglement. In this article, we give a thorough analysis of QML and QDL algorithms, discussing their underlying ideas, benefits over conventional models, and potential uses. We talk about the difficulties these algorithms face, such as noisy quantum hardware, constrained qubit resources, training and optimisation issues, input representation and data encoding problems, and limited interpretability. Additionally, we look at current developments and lines of inquiry that aim to address these issues, including hybrid classical-quantum methods, error-mitigating techniques, better data representation techniques, quantum transfer learning, and resource optimisation.

articleTitle: Quantum-Improved Weather Forecasting: Integrating Quantum Machine Learning for Precise Prediction and Disaster Mitigation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: In numerous industries, weather forecasting is essential for making informed decisions and mitigating the effects of extreme weather events. The complexity and chaos of weather systems, however, place restrictions on standard procedures, leading to errors and significant threats. We suggest the Quantum Improved Weather Forecast framework, which combines quantum machine learning methods with conventional methodologies, to solve these issues. By using quantum algorithms including quantum support vector machines, quantum neural networks, and quantum clustering, the QWF framework seeks to improve accuracy. Despite a few drawbacks, the QWF framework provides a method to revolutionize weather forecasting by enhancing prediction accuracy and facilitating improved catastrophe preparedness. It may prevent fatalities, safeguard critical infrastructure, and promote sustainable growth.

articleTitle: DQNdot: A Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Object Tracking in UAV-Enabled Aerial Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object tracking enables various applications in diverse domains, such as surveillance, traffic scrutiny, and search and rescue. However, it presents a formidable challenge that necessitates the proficiency to trail objects under arduous circumstances. In this paper, Deep Q Networks on dynamic object tracking (DQNdot) are presented, encompassing the ensuing components: You only look once (YOLOv8) that spotlights objects in video frames, UAV for Multi-Object Tracking (UAVMOT) traces objects in video frames employing the Kalman filter and Hungarian method. Subsequently, the prioritizing module is also advanced to prioritize things that are more liable to be seamlessly traced. This module harnesses a range of factors to appraise the probability of an object being efficaciously traced, such as its size, speed, and appearance. Deep Q network(DQN) endows the capability to trail resourcefully, learn and adapt to the environment. DQNdot has accomplished 92% accuracy of prophesying the results for pursuit. It transcends all the other frameworks as it can proficiently track as many targets as required.

articleTitle: A New Systematic Network Intrusion Detection System Using Deep Belief Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: This study discusses a Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) leveraging Deep Belief Networks to classify network traffic into multiple categories. By stacking Multiple Restricted Boltzmann Machines, the NIDS model fosters a Deep Belief Network-a generative graphical model. This implied approach is particularly good at identifying and identifying high-dimensional representations. Using Gibbs Sampling and the Contrastive Divergence method, the Deep Belief Network is first pre-trained unsupervised before being fine-tuned supervised. Our research study utilized the CICIDS2018 dataset to train and assess the effectiveness of our proposed DBN technique. Our empirical findings show that our two-phase training technique not only maintains impressive performance against other types of assaults, but also dramatically improves detection accuracy when comprehending samples of peculiar attacks.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Review On Two-Stage Object Detection Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Two-stage object detection algorithms have gained significant attention in computer vision due to their robustness and accuracy in detecting objects in images. These algorithms consist of two main stages: region proposal generation and object classification/localization. The region proposal stage efficiently generates a diverse set of candidate object regions using various techniques, narrowing down the search space. In the second stage, deep convolutional neural networks extract discriminative features from the proposed regions, enabling precise object classification and localization. These algorithms have demonstrated impressive performance in complex scenes with occlusions, scale variations, and multiple objects. However, they have limitations such as slower inference speeds, increased computational complexity, and the need for additional training steps. To address these limitations, more efficient algorithms like single-stage detectors have emerged. Two-stage object detection algorithms offer a powerful framework for accurate and robust object detection, and ongoing research aims to refine and improve these algorithms, expanding the capabilities of computer vision applications.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Approach for Prioritized Heterogeneous Object Tracking in UAV Swarms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Deep Reinforcement learning(DRL) has recently showcased its boundless potential in Multi-agent collaboration. There exist DRL-based models that strive to unravel the Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) Multi-target tracking predicaments, however, the conundrum of tracing desired targets persists as most research endeavors solely focus on the agents’ policies while neglecting the dynamic environment, which harbors elusive and unpredictable targets. The proposed model executes Prioritized Heterogeneous Object Tracking (PHOT) using DRL, to furnish a solution for preferred Multi-target tracking by upholding the policy of UAV swarms. Tracking preferred targets assumes paramount importance as these targets necessitate meticulous monitoring within the ever-changing environmental backdrop, particularly during surveillance missions employing UAV swarms, which can harness the full potential of the UAV swarms in real-time. A YOLO v4-based algorithm is put forth, which can trail prioritized targets in a tracking by detection paradigm. To maintain the policy of UAV swarms, a dueling double deep Q-learning algorithm is deployed, complemented by a reward function that stimulates UAVs to track the preferred targets instantaneously. The UAVDT dataset is employed for the simulations, and the results evince that PHOT exhibits robustness, suitable for deployment in a real-time environment, amassing a highly commendable average cumulative reward over time, and enabling actions predicated on unidentical prioritized targets.

articleTitle: Extraction and Upadation of Alumni Information from Web Profiles Using Web Scraping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Alumni are the graduates of Higher Education Institutes (HEI). They become vital asset for the alma mater to attain the Institutional Advancements (IA). This paper proposes the centralized applied framework for the management of alumni within the institutions. The main objective of this project is to build a bridge between the alumni’s and institutions with an information retrieval platform called Almadatum. The purpose of Almadatum is to track the readily accessible alumni information at college, and this data has much importance when it comes to any Accreditation Councils. The presented system can generate the reports of the alumni in the identified characteristics and requirements. Updating the information of an alumnus or alumnae become easy now because of the interface we have proposed. The system is associated with web scraping and web crawling techniques for gathering and updating alumni information which makes it reliable. The usage of web scraping made the system even more advanced and effective, having a system which leverages scraping social media profiles of alumni such as LinkedIn to provide accurate data is a beneficial advancement to IA. This portal has been designed with many features few from them like: Alumni can donate to the institutions, view the conducted meeting as well as the upcoming meetings with alumnus. The portal does also contains a communication page similar to social network site for alumni through which they can view, edit, update their details. Alumni can post job vacancies by using communication page and all the posted vacancies are visible in communication page itself, this can facilitate current students who are searching for a job. Overall ALMADATUM is serving the purpose of maintaining alumni engagement for HEI.

articleTitle: A Fast Image Encryption Technique Based on Chaotic Maps and Image Divisional Techniques for Multiple Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The proliferation of communication networks has led to a surge in the exchange of multimedia information through unsecured channels. Therefore, it is necessary to safeguard multimedia images during transmission through unsecured communication channels. The paper aims to propose a scheme for fast encryption of images that utilizes chaos-based maps and image divisional techniques. The method involves the initial division of the image into four sub-images. Next, a pixel-permutation process is executed on the pixels of each sub-image utilising four distinct indexing sequences based on chaotic maps. The permutated outputs are subjected to a pixel diffusion operation utilising four distinct key images based on chaotic maps. Finally, the encrypted output is produced by joining all the dispersed outputs. Based on the computer simulations and analysis on security, it has been determined that the suggested method is competent of securely and efficiently encrypting images.

articleTitle: Node Level Tracking for a Self-Defending Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The field of cyber security is constantly evolving as new threats emerge, and traditional security measures often are reactive in nature, leading to networks being vulnerable to sophisticated attacks. A self-defending and anticipatory network aims to address this problem by proactively identifying potential threats, anticipating attacks, and automatically responding to them in real time. In this paper, the authors suggest a new kind of decentralized architecture for a self-defending network wherein each node in the network maintains a data structure called Failure Probability Table or FPT to keep track of other nodes behavior. The value in the FPT for each node will be decided on the basis of real time machine learning algorithms. The FPT values help in isolating the node, and also pre-emptive rerouting to minimize the effects on the network based on certain thresholds. This novel approach of each node having its own FPT values has the potential to substantially enhance the robustness of network security, effectively countering sophisticated attacks and fortifying against evolving threats in a proactive manner.

articleTitle: A Diffusion-Only Image Encryption System for High-Speed Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The widespread and growing utilisation of digital images has made image encryption a crucial concern, garnering significant attention from researchers. Regrettably, the development and study of fast encryption schemes for colour images are currently lacking. This paper proposes a specifically designed colour image encryption system for high-speed applications, utilising only diffusion techniques. The proposed technique employs a set of five Piece-wise Linear Chaotic Maps (PWLCM) with different first values and control factors to execute the image encryption operation. The SHA-256 hashing is employed for the initialization of first values and control factors in PWLCM system. The technique involves initially separating the colour image into its three colour components. Subsequently, the three components are horizontally concatenated. Next, the generation of three key images is achieved by employing the three PWLCM systems, each with distinct key parameters. Subsequently, these three key images are concatenated together. Furthermore, the concatenated outputs are partitioned into blocks with dimensions of $(1 \times 3)$. The process involves performing a bit-XORing diffusion process on the concatenated outputs of the selected blocks of the colour component and the key image. The block selection operation is performed using two distinct PWLCM systems. The diffused blocks are ultimately merged to produce the ciphertext. Based on the analysis on security and experimental outputs, it has been determined, the described method successfully encrypts the color photos of different sizes while ensuring their security.

articleTitle: Secure Firmware Update Architecture for IoT Devices using Blockchain and PUF
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The utilization of embedded devices within the Internet of Things (IoT) landscape is projected to become increasingly widespread. These compact IoT devices operate autonomously and interact with one another seamlessly, necessitating robust security measures to safeguard their operations from potential attacks. This paper addresses the security implications of updating firmware on embedded devices within an IoT environment. To tackle this challenge, a firmware update architecture is proposed that combines blockchain technology and Physical Unclonable Function (PUF) to establish a secure framework for verifying firmware versions, validating firmware integrity, and facilitating the download of the most recent firmware binaries onto embedded devices. If the firmware is outdated, the device is first authenticated by utilizing PuF’s Challenge-Response Pairs (CRPs). Subsequently, the device initiates a firmware update request within a blockchain network and awaits a response to determine the availability of its firmware version. If available, the new version is then downloaded and updated. This scheme establishes a robust framework that guarantees upto-date versions of embedded device firmware while mitigating potential attacks targeting known firmware vulnerabilities within embedded devices.

articleTitle: Advancement in Plant Pathology using Image Segmentation and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The study recommends utilizing image processing techniques and a dual-layer CNN for analyzing datasets related to root rot. The research emphases on detecting and diagnosing root rot over Machine Learning and image processing. In Past Authors had worked on one plant disease situations using openly available schema. However, this research incorporates actual-images taken from many farms in Village Rancharda in Ahmedabad District. The proposed model trains and tests on more than 50,000 images of 10 different plants. These images are classified into 36 definite classes, distinguishing healthy and diseased types based on disease labels. To refine the image data and enhance the diseased portion, image pre-processing techniques such as simple segmentation using HSV threshold, and segmentation using breadth first search is proposed deep learning model were compared. The resolution of images was adjusted to ensure consistency across the dataset. For image processing, a SWMAD technique was employed, creating 6channel images that were stacked onto the original image. The proposed model exhibited superior performance during validation, achieving an accuracy of up to 0.9791%. Moreover, the model was converted into a TFLite model, enabling its use in client applications without requiring a server. In this case, the model was implemented in an Android application.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Instructional Practices: Using Behavior Detection and Model Assignment Techniques to Inform Teaching Strategies for School Education
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: An increasingly common method for assessing students’ performance on tests is automated grading. It might potentially free up time for teachers and provide students with fast feedback so they can see where they need to improve. For better learning outcomes, automated grading must be utilized in conjunction with other instructional strategies. In this study, we provide Python codes for factor analysis-based automated grading to analyze students’ performance on tests. The code first loads the evaluation data as a matrix with each row denoting a student and each column denoting an evaluation item. After that, we use factor analysis to find latent variables that affect student performance. We establish a grading system in which each letter grade is assigned a specific threshold score. Afterwards, we assign each student a grade based on their factor scores, which are determined by adding their results for each latent factor. Each student’s grade and overall score are output by the code. Additionally, our automated grading system demonstrated the ability to spot trends in student performance that could guide teaching strategies. Our computerised grading system can potentially save time and give students rapid feedback, but it must be used in concert with other instructional strategies to guarantee successful learning outcomes. Our study emphasises the significance of employing automated grading to supplement human evaluators rather than to replace them. In order to further tailor learning experiences for students, future study might examine the use of automated grading in conjunction with other behaviour detection and model assignment strategies. Additionally, the development of increasingly complex algorithms might make it possible for automated grading systems to spot trends in student performance that are difficult for human assessors to spot.

articleTitle: Exploring Data as Quantum Bits: Analysis of Quantum Image Encoding Patterns for NISQ era
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The generall efficiency of a computational system, be it simple or complex, presentation of the data plays a crucial role in getting the most out of it. Classical information theory, quantum mechanics, and computer science collectively influence Quantum Information in comprehending how information can be encoded, transmitted, and modified using quantum systems. Quantum mechanics allows quantum information to incorporate a variety of properties, such as quantum encoding of classical information, storing coherent details in quantum superpositions, quantum computations and entanglement, which occurs when two or more qubits become highly correlated and share an unbreakable quantum state. There are numerous barriers and constraints in the broad field of quantum computation, ranging from dealing with Decoherence to ensuring error correction. Moreover, the qubit, a fundamental computational unit, is challenging to create, manipulate, and store. To ensure the quality of the Quantum Algorithms, the area of quantum data encoding has been thoroughly researched and explored as relevant results can be obtained by adequate encoding. In this paper, we reviewed the terminology and physical modeling of qubits, as well as the encoding approaches used to transform data from classical to quantum models. Furthermore, different encoding schemes for Quantum Image Processing were explored to determine the efficiency of quantum pixel representation(QPIXL) framework for effective application in NISQ era.

articleTitle: LTV-Backed E-Signatures Using Post-Quantum Cryptography
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Due to concerns over the evolving quantum computing scenario and its potential threat to existing cryptosystems, including Public-Key Infrastructure (PKI) used in electronic signatures, there is a need to enhance the eSign components with quantum-resistant algorithms. One such algorithm is CrystalsDilithium, based on lattice cryptography, which can perform PKI operations in the eSign system. In addition to being resistant to quantum attacks, Long-Term Validation (LTV) is also utilized to ensure the validity of a document for an extended period. This is achieved by referring to PAdES/CAdES profiles and a time stamping service, which provides an accurate and trustworthy record of when a particular electronic document, file, or transaction was created, modified, or sent. Given the significance of eSign as a crucial digital service worldwide, migrating to post-quantum components will strengthen the system’s security. Therefore, the proposed research provides implementation, analysis and experimentation to ensure the eSign system components are robust against quantum computing threats.

articleTitle: Enhanced Ant Colony Optimization with Dynamic Evaporation Rate (EACO-DE): An Intelligent Congestion Control System in IoV Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Internet of Vehicle (IoV) is a combined form of Internet of Things (IoT) and Vehicular Ad-hoc Network (VANET). Its fundamental goal is to increase the service quality of Intelligent Transportation System (ITS). The dynamic nature of IoV such as high dynamic topology, high mobility of vehicles, etc. are some of the factors that causes more congestion thus reducing the efficiency of routing. Many algorithms were designed to obtain the shortest path from the source to the destination. Choosing of Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm is one of the best ways to obtain the shortest path. In this paper, an Enhanced Ant Colony Optimization with Dynamic Evaporation rate (EACODE) algorithm is proposed to obtain the congestion-free optimized path which reduces the travel time, travel cost and traffic problems. Instead of fixed evaporation rate, it dynamic predicts the pheromone evaporation rate with the help of run time metrics to avoid the congested paths thus improving the efficiency of the travel. The simulation results show that the proposed EACO-DE algorithm improves the efficiency of the routing compared with primitive Ant Colony Optimization (ACO) algorithm and Enhanced Hybrid Ant Colony Optimization Routing Protocol (EHACORP) under various performance metrics.

articleTitle: IOT Based Road Accident Detection and Prevention System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: According to statistics conducted by the WHO (World Health Organization), road traffic injuries claim the lives of more than 50% of people each year. where head injuries are the primary cause of fatality for riders of two-wheelers. These death ratios can be reduced by making helmet use mandatory. Wearing a helmet can reduce the number of deadly wounds by 75%. Furthermore, according to WHO, the likelihood of driving while intoxicated is increasing globally, which increases the risk of a serious traffic collision. Additionally, there are certain rural locations in the world with lower human traffic. Due to the emergency services’ response time being delayed, riders in this situation lost their lives. Despite the fact that a number of awareness campaigns have been launched and laws have been enacted in the interests of the populace, people continue to break the law, including those prohibiting driving while intoxicated. therefore, a problem-solving strategy is to design an original prose paper on “ Use of safety equipment is required for detecting alcohol and battery fires with an embedded system. ”. The paper’s extra features include the use of GSM technology, which notifies the owner in the event of a fire or drunken accident.

articleTitle: Exploring Cognitive and Affective Processing Based on Webcam-Based Heartrate Activity
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Without the use of electrodes, a pleasant physiological assessment can be achieved by remotely measuring the heart pulse and detecting the health status of the heart. However, current methods are not automated, are prone to motion artifacts, expensive and few devices that require a medical expert to handle and determine heartrate. We solve these concerns by introducing a novel methodology in this research. Once the initial heartrate is determined, the user is exposed to different images representing different scenarios such as pleasant, scary, creepy, scenic. We then analyzed the changing patterns of the user’s heartrate at different time points as the user viewed each photo. In this study, we monitored the heartrates of individuals with different range of ages and skin tones and stored them as a dataset. The published dataset was then contrasted with this dataset. Finally, a general report on the heart condition was produced and a graph showing the various patterns of a person’s heartrate was created.

articleTitle: Metamorphosing Teaching and Learning with Python: A Practical Guide for Teachers Employing Text Data Analysis Using the Bag of Words (BoW) Model
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: This research explores the application of the Bag of Words (BoW) model for text data analysis with the goal of enhancing teaching-learning in the classroom. The BoW model expresses text as a “bag” of its individual words while ignoring word order. The study covers the use of the BoW model toward the creation of intelligent teaching systems. These systems identify areas where students may be having difficulty and offer focused feedback and guidance by examining the language used by students as they work through an issue or subject. The paper uses snippets of Python code as examples and their outputs to demonstrate how the BoW model can be used to improve learning outcomes. The BoW model’s importance in assessing educational resources, developing intelligent tutoring programmes, and analysing student writing is greatly emphasised in the paper.

articleTitle: Mitigating Health Risks and Ensuring Safe Video Streaming Environments through Automated Video Content Moderation
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Automated content moderation systems have become essential for maintaining a safe and healthy online environment with the ever-increasing amount of video content on the internet and social media platforms. Individuals are likely to see videos containing flashing lights that can trigger seizures, nudity, or videos that may evoke extreme emotions like anxiety, frustration, or despair. In this paper, we propose a comprehensive content moderation solution that incorporates several features. The system features epileptic seizure recognition, emotional dysregulation prevention, and kid-safe mode. Epilepsy is a chronic neurological disorder affecting millions worldwide. Various factors can trigger seizures, including flashing lights, which are prevalent in video content. The system analyzes videos for trigger segments and skips them to non-trigger segments, mitigating the risk of seizures in individuals with epilepsy. The proposed algorithm uses a sophisticated analysis of the differences in luminosity between each video frame. It identifies areas that represent potential seizure-inducing segments due to their high density of big changes in luminosity. Similarly, when a video triggers strong emotions, the emotional dysregulation prevention mechanism recognizes it and alerts the user with an emotional summary of the video. The emotional dysregulation algorithm uses a deep learning model for facial emotion identification based on the VGG16 architecture. In kid-safe mode, the nudity detection algorithm uses CNN architecture, recognizes explicit content, and blocks users, especially children, from seeing it. The system displays notifications and alerts to parents to establish restrictions on the content their children can access. The proposed mechanisms prevent potential harm to users with specific vulnerabilities and provide parents with tools to ensure a safe online streaming environment for their kids.

articleTitle: Blockchain and Deep Learning-Based Models for Crypto Price Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Blockchain technology is becoming more and more popular because of its decentralized, unchangeable, safe, and anonymous characteristics. Cryptocurrencies, which have seen tremendous development and market capitalization in recent years, are where they are most widely used. Individuals, organizations, and businesses are all making significant investments in this area. In contrast to conventional commodities markets, the cryptocurrency market is more volatile, unstable, and unpredictable. It can be affected by a variety of technological, emotional, and legal variables. Although there has been a lot of research towards predicting cryptocurrency prices, many of the current methods are not appropriate for use in real time.
