To solve this, we suggest using the Python-based LGBM Neural network model to forecast market changes in real-time and reduce investor losses. The outcomes of our evaluation of this strategy using reference datasets show its dependability. Thus, over the past ten years, researchers from a variety of domains have used neural networks as an efficient data mining method.

articleTitle: Characterizing and Classifying Android Malware: A High-Level Feature Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: We present a novel framework for characterizing and classifying Android malware based on high-level abstract features. Our research highlights the limitations of traditional approaches that directly rely on low-level implementation units such as Android API calls, permissions, system properties, and intents to classify malware into different categories. To address these constraints, we introduce a method for malware classification that leverages high-level attributes rooted in the MITRE ATT&CK (Adversarial Tactics, Techniques, and Common Knowledge) framework. This strategy offers a more generalized portrayal of malware behavior, reducing reliance on particular implementation technologies, while also establishing a uniform terminology for articulating malware conduct. In our study, we developed a classification scheme for Android malware based on the techniques defined in the mobile ATT&CK framework. We accomplished this in two steps: first, we mapped various mobile ATT&CK techniques to low-level implementation units, such as Android API calls, permissions, system properties, and intents. Second, we characterized seven families of Android malware using ATT&CK techniques and used them to classify these malware families. Our focus was on 33 ATT&CK techniques out of the 70 currently present in the mobile ATT&CK framework, and we created a mapping for each of these techniques in terms of implementation units. By using only ATT&CK techniques as features for classification, we significantly reduced the number of features used by our classifier compared to current classifiers that use hundreds of low-level features. Our model not only improve overall classification results, but also allows for modification of the low-level mapping without the need to retrain the classifier. Through the correlation of ATT&CK techniques with low-level implementation components, we managed to notably decrease the count of features employed by the classifier, all the while attaining an accuracy exceeding 97%.

articleTitle: Blackhole Attack Detection and Analysis of Routing Protocol in the Context of Internet of Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Vehicles, sensors, and communication technology make up the Internet of Vehicles (IoV). Its main function is to allow vehicles to communicate seamlessly. Connectivity between all these things is crucial. Therefore, routing is the Adhoc on Demand Distance Vector (AODV) routing protocol efficiently connects vehicles and other components. Blackhole routing attacks in vehicular networks pose an imminent threat to communication and data security. The impact of black hole attacks on AODV routing protocol is the focus of this research. Analyzing performance metrics such as Packet Delivery Ratio (PDR), End-to-End Delay (EED), and Throughput during a black hole attack with those during normal operation has been done. We have used NS2.35 for our simulations and acquisition of results, and conducted one-way Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) tests to establish statistical significance. In this research we have used the IEEE 802.11p standard and performs statistical testing to look for proof of blackhole attacks. In addition, a new technique based on AODV mac packet analysis is presented in this study for detecting blackhole attacks in IoV.

articleTitle: En-BB84: Advancements in Secure Quantum Key Distribution with Improved Error Resilience and Built-in Authentication
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a method that enables secure communication between two parties by applying the ideas of quantum physics. By minimizing information leakage that can happen during the key generation process, privacy amplification is a technique used to improve the security of QKD. The technique involves processing the raw key obtained from QKD through a randomization procedure to remove any residual information that may have been leaked during the quantum transmission. While privacy amplification can significantly improve the security of QKD, the effectiveness of the technique is limited by the quality of the initial raw key. The BB84 QKD protocol has been improved with the proposed En-BB84 protocol, which includes built-in authentication and integrity checks. The En-BB84 protocol ensures secure distribution of secret keys and protects against tampering by attackers. Key distillation and error correction techniques are employed to extract a shorter, more secure shared secret key and correct errors introduced during qubit transmission. The protocol utilizes a four-state QKD approach, expanding on the traditional two-state scheme of BB84. A simulation of the En-BB84 protocol is demonstrated using a quantum circuit implemented with Qiskit in Python. The circuit employs various gates and operations, including Hadamard, CX, controlled swap, and RZ gates, to achieve encoding and error correction. Furthermore, we have designed a better protocol with improved error rates by incorporating improvisations on the BB84 protocol. Experimental results indicate the successful integration of the B92 error correction scheme into the modified BB84 protocol, enhancing the security and performance of QKD systems.

articleTitle: An Effective, Permutation-only, Bit-Level Image Encryption System Using Chaotic Maps
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The widespread and growing utilization of digital images has elevated the significance of image encryption as a crucial concern, garnering significant attention from researchers. Regrettably, the current state of image encryption schemes lacks comprehensive development and research. This article presents a new image encryption system that uses only permutations and works at the bit level. The system incorporates chaotic maps to enhance its effectiveness. The method begins by executing the bit-plane generation process, which is then followed by the bit-plane concatenation operation. The bit-planes are individually subjected to bit-shuffling using distinct Logistic chaotic maps (LM) with varying key values. The shuffled outputs are vertically concatenated and then horizontally concatenated to execute the final stage of the bit-level shuffling operation. The output obtained from concatenation is subjected to a two-step shuffling process. First, a row-shuffling operation is performed, followed by a column-shuffling operation. Both shuffling operations are carried out using a separate LM system. The shuffled output is subjected to bit-plane separation and subsequently combined to produce the cipher image. The hash-based key values of LM systems enhance the method’s resistance towards the selected-plaintext and selected-ciphertext attacks. Based on the computer simulations and security analysis conducted, it has been determined that the proposed method has been demonstrated to be effective in encrypting images securely and efficiently.

articleTitle: Hybrid Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: The purpose of (IDS) is to protect digital data from cyber threats. By quickly distinguishing and reacting to risks, IDS minimizes possible damage to systems and data. However, it can suffer from performance issues, such as delayed warnings and compromised accuracy. To solve this problem, our approach combines IDS with machine learning and a deep learning approach. It uses agglomerative hierarchical clustering and random forest (RF) algorithms for classification, supported by recurrent neural networks (RNN) for attack classification. Their implementation in MATLAB allows the classification of events. Evaluation with the NSL-KDD and CIS-IDS2017 datasets showed a high true positive rate (TPR) and successful detection of minority attacks, confirming its effectiveness.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Boosting Algorithms to Detect the Fake User Profiles on Instagram
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Social media use has become a significant part of every person’s daily life during the past several years. These social media sites support in the three Cs: creating, connecting, and communicating with others. Nearly 4.8 billion people use social media globally, according to use data. There are millions of individuals worldwide that spend the majority of their time on social networking websites. A variety of threats, such as bogus profiles, account hacking, safety and security problems, might arise with an increase in usage. The most popular and broadly used social networking site is Instagram. The purpose of the following paper is to identify phoney accounts of people on Instagram using machine learning boosting techniques. We developed a new set of algorithms described as ADB-CB, which includes extra tree classifier, cat boost, and Ada boost, for recognising or detecting these false user profiles. Additionally, various feature selection and reduction strategies are then used. Kaggle Instagram datasets were taken into account when evaluating the model. Catboost, Adaboost, and the extra tree classifier all performed with accuracy ratings of 96, 91.87, and 93.78 respectively. Of all boosting algorithms, the Catboost had the highest level of accuracy of 96.

articleTitle: Air Quality Prediction using Automated ML
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Quantum Technologies, Communications, Computing, Hardware and Embedded Systems Security (iQ-CCHESS)
abstract: Air pollution has grown to be one of the world’s most serious health and environmental issues. The broad range of gases like sulfur dioxide, carbon monoxide, etc which are released into the atmosphere due to the incomplete combustion of fossil fuels results in air pollution. These pollutants must be monitored carefully in order to find out the changes over time and to provide these data for predicting future conditions. Therefore records collected and processed based on those subjects have grown to be an important research location. The main aim of this work is to make use of Automated ML and investigate various machine-learning approaches for air quality forecasting. It makes use of particulate matter using the present and historical values with the combination of values that is readily available. Here, by implementing the proposed parameter-reducing formulation using Automated ML it achieved a better performance than the standard regression models. The proposed model resulted in 80% prediction accuracy when empirically evaluated with UCI data set on pollutant prediction.
